articles.title: Trump’s unprecedented $37B failure exposed as secret meeting details leak: report
articles.description: President Donald Trump's escalating military campaign against Iran is achieving the “opposite” of its intended effect, according to a senior U.S. official cited in a New York Times report Saturday. “The official said the strikes have the opposite effect of what is intended, keeping Iran cohesive and allowing Iranian leaders to focus attention on an external threat,” the Times’ report reads. The assessment came after insiders leaked details to the Times about a Friday meeting between Trump and his top advisers and Cabinet members, where officials weighed whether or not to escalate the war further. According to the Times, few, if any, in Trump's inner circle believed intensifying the bombing campaign was wise. A separate senior official who was briefed on the discussion expressed doubts that resuming major combat operations would push Iran back to the table at all. The “private deliberations” focused on what officials warned was the Pentagon’s “shrinking inventory of Patriot interceptors and other air defenses,” the Times reported. “Gen. Dan Caine, the chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, has cautioned privately that resuming major combat operations against Iran was doable but that it would dangerously deplete interceptors available to the military’s Central Command, which is responsible for operations in the Middle East, the officials said,” the Times’ report reads. Earlier this week, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth told a congressional committee that Trump’s deeply unpopular war against Iran had cost taxpayers $37.5 billion so far. The internal skepticism adds to a growing list of signs that the administration's approach to Iran isn't producing the results Trump has publicly promised, even as the financial and human costs of the conflict continue to climb.

articles.title: Onlookers rejoice as federal court slaps down Trump’s attack on mail-in ballots
articles.description: A federal court dealt a major blow to President Donald Trump’s efforts to limit the use of mail-in ballots for the upcoming midterm elections, sparking a chorus of celebration among Trump administration critics. On Saturday, The U.S. First Circuit Court of Appeals rejected the Trump administration’s attempt to block a lower court order that prohibited the U.S. Postal Service (USPS) from carrying out the president’s executive order on mail-in ballots. Signed in March, Trump’s executive order would require states to send the federal government a list of all its voters it plans on sending absentee ballots. The USPS could then refuse to deliver mail-in ballots to any voters not on the list, essentially forcing states to fork over private and detailed voter information to the executive branch. With Trump’s efforts to restrict mail-in ballots hitting another hurdle on Saturday, a number of onlookers celebrated, including Kristen McKnight, an advocate for survivors of abuse and a retired clinical psychologist. “Good news,” McKnight wrote Saturday in a social media post on X. Craig Goedecke, an amateur weather observer and retired photojournalist, not only celebrated the federal court’s decision Saturday, but argued that the ruling boded poorly for Trump’s other top priority, the SAVE Act, his controversial voter ID bill. “Back the F off from our mail ballots. Your SAVE Act crap is over. The First [Circuit] Court denied your request to allow the USPS to move forward,” Goedecke wrote Saturday in a social media post on X. “It’s illegal. Our election. Our votes. Our mail-in ballots. Not yours. You are not rigging our election... and the Senate is not passing it.” Good news.👇 https://t.co/zRdfxQkw8I — Kristen McKnight (@kristenmcknight) July 25, 2026

articles.title: Trump ordered military not to conduct strikes in Iran Friday
articles.description: President Trump directed the U.S. military not to conduct new strikes in Iran on Friday, breaking a nearly two-week streak of daily attacks, two sources with knowledge of the decision said. Why it matters: The president's directive came after he approved daily strikes over the previous 13 days. It is unclear if Trump's order on Friday was a one-off or whether the lull will continue. Trump's decision reflects both his willingness to provide more space for diplomacy and a recognition that — short of a return to major combat operations — the current level of U.S. strikes has reached the limit of its effectiveness. If Trump orders a return to strikes, the U.S. military can mobilize on relatively short notice. The U.S. military is still preparing plans for a possible return to major combat operations, but Trump hasn't given orders to move in that direction, the sources said. The White House did not respond to a request for comment. Driving the news: Every afternoon for the last two weeks, Trump has approved strike plans submitted by the military. They were conducted within hours. On Friday, Trump received a similar plan but did not give a green light. Instead, he directed the military not to conduct strikes, the sources said. Shortly after he gave the Friday directive, Trump told reporters at the White House that he has the option of continuing strikes or even escalating them, including "knocking out everything they have." But he made clear that he thinks the "smarter strategy" is to "make a deal" with Iran. "We're talking to [the Iranians] right now. I think they're getting more and more serious as the days go by. We're locked and loaded and ready to go, but we're talking to them," Trump said. Later on Friday, during his remarks at the White House Correspondents Association dinner, Trump said he didn't think Iran is ready to make a deal at the moment, "but I'm willing to listen." State of play: Trump's order to hold fire was given several hours after an Omani delegation arrived in Tehran Friday for talks on a new arrangement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Two regional sources with knowledge of the negotiations said progress has been made in the talks and that an agreement between Oman and Iran could be reached over the weekend. President Trump would then have to decide whether to accept the proposed deal.

articles.title: PML-N's 'gift': Buses promised by Maryam reach AJK as election commission warns against violating electoral code
articles.description: MUZAFFARABAD: E-buses announced by the PML-N as a “gift” arrived in Muzaffarabad on Saturday as the Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) Election Commission warned against violating the code of conduct for election campaigns. The AJK Election Commission warned that it would not allow any individual or institution to violate the code of conduct, a day after former prime minister Nawaz Sharif and Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz announced development schemes, including the “gift” of 10 e-buses at election rallies in Muzaffarabad and Mirpur. CM Maryam confirmed on Saturday afternoon that the green buses had arrived in the regional capital, sharing a video that showed several of the vehicles bearing posters with her picture. The PML-N’s Friday announcement had not gone well with the PPP, which described it as “political bribery”. It then approached the Election Commission, urging it to take notice of what it termed a violation of the election code of conduct. Subsequently, an Election Commission spokesperson said federal and provincial ministers were free to participate in electioneering in AJK but could not use official protocol, government resources or the state machinery for electoral purposes. The spokesperson warned that the announcement of any new development scheme, financial package, public facility or welfare project during the election campaign would amount to a violation of the code of conduct. Any vehicles, equipment, relief goods or other facilities sent by the federal or provincial governments during the election period would be confiscated and action taken in accordance with the law, the statement added. The spokesperson urged all ministers, candidates and political parties to strictly observe the code of conduct to ensure free, fair and transparent elections and maintain public confidence in the electoral process. Meanwhile, AJK Secretary Information Muhammad Rashid Hanif and Director Information Tariq Jamil Durrani urged journalists and media organisations to ensure responsible, impartial and professional coverage of the elections. In a joint message, they called on the media to publish only verified and balanced information, avoid rumours and inflammatory content, and adhere to the Election Commission’s code of conduct and journalistic ethics. They also urged users of social media platforms to refrain from sharing unverified or misleading material that could undermine the electoral process or disturb public order. PPP accuses PML-N of ‘political bribery’ Separately, PPP Secretary General Nayyer Hussain Bukhari met with AJK Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Justice (retd) Ghulam Mustafa Mughal on Saturday over the issue of pre-poll development schemes. He urged the CEC to take notice of the Punjab government’s decision to hand over 10 electric buses bearing the photographs of CM Maryam to the AJK administration. He said the PPP considered the act as “political bribery” and alleged that the PML-N was trying to “buy the AJK elections” by using tax money of the people of Punjab. “After the announcement of the election schedule, any such step by any executive amounts to a clear violation of election laws,” he asserted. Bukhari questioned whether the buses were purchased “from the account of Jati Umra”, and asked the CEC to take notice of the matter. He also submitted a request for issuance of a no-objection certificate (NOC) for the PPP to run a “motivation service” in connection with the party manifesto and election campaign in AJK, and urged the CEC to decide early on the party’s appeal. Matters related to the AJK general elections 2026, the code of conduct, and permission letters required for political parties also came under discussion. In a statement, PPP Central Spokesperson Shazia Marri said Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari was striving for a bright and empowered future for every Kashmiri. She said the PPP chairman had raised the slogan of the right to rule, right to property and right to employment for the people of Kashmir, adding “this is not a crime”. Marri asked PML-N to present its plan of action for Kashmir to the people instead of attacking political allies. “The people of Kashmir do not want allegations by political parties; they want solutions to their problems,” she said. She said Nawaz was repeating the same old narrative on which he “could not deliver despite being in power three times”.
